dedupe_keys.name: tinygs open citizen network of lora ground stations receiving satellite telemetry

description: TinyGS is an open-source global network of small ground stations, built by volunteers from low-cost ESP32 LoRa boards, that receive telemetry from satellites and share it through the TinyGS web application. Its home page reports more than 8,750 members, more than 2,250 active stations and more than 65 million telemetry packets received, and presents the network as a citizen science contribution to space situational awareness, tracking objects in orbit and predicting their positions. Coverage: global, where volunteers operate stations; mainly small satellites that transmit with LoRa. Format and access: packets and station data are shown in the TinyGS web application; free to join and browse. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): station software GPL-3.0; no data licence stated in the TinyGS terms. Caveats: coverage and uptime depend on volunteers; the data describe small satellites' telemetry, not the large navigation or communications constellations; bulk export options were not read. Simulation uses: evidence of small satellite activity and reception for studies of space-based services and ground segment resilience. Related records: SatNOGS DB (data-satnogs-db) is a larger open ground station network and transmitter database, and CelesTrak (data-celestrak-gp-satcat) gives the orbital elements.
